verses.1: And the people became very sad in the ears of Jehovah. Jehovah heard them, and a fire from Him burned among them. Jehovah consumed everything in the camp.
verses.2: And the people cried out to Moses. Moses prayed to Yahweh, and the fire disappeared.
verses.3: And they called that place “Tav’era”, because in that place, the LORD would bring fire.
verses.4: And the Ark, in whose midst there was God, became filled with anger. Then the Israelites also wept and mourned. They said, “Who will eat us when we are no longer able to survive?”
verses.5: We remember the dishes that were eaten in Egypt: honey, honey cakes, goats’ meat, lamb, and other delicacies.
verses.6: And now, let us be free from all this sorrow. There’s nothing left but to look into our own eyes.
verses.7: And its fruit is like a seed of wheat; and its eyes are like those of a bird.
verses.8: The people scattered and gathered together, and they ate their food in the open air or in their homes. They also made various kinds of dishes from it. The taste of these dishes was like that of honey.
verses.9: And in the rain that fell on the camp at night, the mud covered it all.
verses.10: And Moses heard the people crying out to their families, each person trying to get to the entrance of the tent. Then God’s anger was greatly stirred in Moses’ eyes.
verses.11: And Moses said to the LORD, “Why do you want them to serve you? Why haven’t you shown me favor in your eyes, so that I could bring this entire people under your rule?”
verses.12: I have given birth to all these people. If I were to say that they are children in your arms, then it would be true, just as a mother carries her child on her arms when she places it on the earth that was promised to her ancestors.
verses.13: From now on, I will give flesh to this entire people, so that they may cry out to me and say, “Give us flesh to eat.”
verses.14: I cannot carry all this people alone, for it’s too much for me.
verses.15: And if you do this to me, then kill me! Please kill me, if I have found favor in your eyes. But I will not see evil in you.
verses.16: And the LORD said to Moses, “Pick seventy men from among the elders of Israel. You know that they are the elders of the people and their leaders. Take them to the tabernacle and let them stand there with you.”
verses.17: And I went down and spoke with you there. I took them from above you, and I placed them on them. Then they carried you along with the rest of the people. You couldn’t carry yourself alone.
verses.18: And to the people he said, “Be holy, for tomorrow you will eat meat. In your homes, you will hear the words of Jehovah: ‘Who will give us meat to eat, since it is good for us in Egypt? So Jehovah will give you meat to eat.”
verses.19: Not one day shall you eat, nor five days, nor ten days, nor twenty days.
verses.20: Until the next new month comes, when he will leave from among you. Then it will be a cause of shame for you, because you have rejected Jehovah who was among you. You will weep before him and say, “Why have we left Egypt?”
verses.21: And Moses said, “Six thousand people who are with me. You said that you would give them food to eat, and they will be able to live for six days.”
verses.22: They would hunt for them in the morning and at dusk. They would also find them if they collected all the fish from the sea.
verses.23: And the LORD said to Moses, “Now the hand of the LORD shall be shortened. You shall see my words no longer.”
verses.24: Moses went out and spoke to the people about the words of God. He gathered seventy men from among the elders of the people, and they stood around the altar.
verses.25: And Jehovah came down in a cloud, and spoke to him. He took fire from the heavens and gave it to those seventy old men. A cloud covered them, and they continued to burn without ever stopping.
verses.26: And two men remained in the camp. The name of one was Eldad, and the name of the other was Medad. Then the wind blew over them. They were in a state of confusion, and they did not leave the camp.
verses.27: And the young man ran and reported to Moses. He said, “Eldad and Medad are coming to the camp.”
verses.28: And Joshua, son of Nun, was one of Moses’ chosen men. He said, “Lord, Moses is like a lamp.”
verses.29: And Moses said to him, “You are the one who will lead me. And who else but you can receive the messages from Jehovah? For Jehovah will give His spirit upon them.”
verses.30: And Moses gathered together the elders of Israel at the camp.
verses.31: And the wind blew from before Jehovah. It brought up the waters from the sea, and it rushed over the camp, in the direction of Yehuah. And it rushed around the edges of the camp, as if it were spreading out across the land.
verses.32: And the people gathered all day and all night, and every day of the following days. They collected enough food to last them for a long time. They gathered twelve oxen, and they prepared a place around the camp for storing their food.
verses.33: The plague still afflicted them both before they could be healed. Even Jehovah was angry with the people, and Jehovah struck the people severely.
verses.34: And they called the name of that place “the Place of Burial”. For there was where the people who were rebellious were buried.
verses.35: From the tombs of the martyrs, the people went out into the courtyards. They were in those courtyards.
